bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity volatility (Aluminum, Steel, Gas) due to West Asia geopolitical tensions; Fuel price hikes impacting rural/urban demand sentiment; Regulatory uncertainty (ABS mandate, EPR draft notification); EV profitability timeline extension due to heavy capex/R&D.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth (scooters/EV/exports) but cautious on short-term margin volatility; Transparent about commodity headwinds exceeding price hikes; Aggressive on capacity expansion to meet demand.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Retail growth outpacing dispatch indicates a rare channel de-stocking phase creating a clean base for FY27; EV loss per unit is declining quarter-on-quarter despite absolute loss increase due to scale; 'Saiyaara' movie product placement drove 120% growth in specific premium variants, highlighting marketing efficacy over pure product specs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Scooters: +48% YoY volume; EV: Volumes up 2.5x YoY; Premium (Harley range): +26% YoY; Exports: +41% YoY (4.02 lakh units, ~₹3,500 cr revenue); Commuter: Market share >90% in entry segments; Parts & Accessories: ₹6,200 cr FY26 (+6% YoY).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Brand slide claims "World's largest motorcycle and scooter company for 25 consecutive years", "manufacturing happiness since 1985", built on "scale, extensive customer reach and four decades of transforming mobility".
- "House of Strategy" sets eight priorities: grow the core (100cc), gain market share in 125cc, win in premium, drive scooter market share, EV leadership, global business, expand parts business, and build a future-fit organisation (development cycle time, best-in-class quality, forecasting & supply agility).
- Domestic Market Share - ICE of 29.0% (+0.3% YoY) in Q1 FY27.
- Global footprint extended to 53 markets with entry into Germany (deck: "Entered Germany (53rd Global market)").
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Parts business] Parts Revenue up 30% YoY (PAM revenue Rs 1,296 Cr in Q1 FY26 to Rs 1,689 Cr in Q1 FY27), with the Hero Genuine Parts distributor network expanded to taluka level for rural accessibility, plus breadth expansion into non-vehicle allied revenue streams and premium riding gear / lifestyle accessories.
- [International launches] Xoom 125 launched in Colombia and Xpulse 210 launched in Nepal; VIDA made its global debut with entry into Nepal, supported by a launch anthem featuring Anna Sharma and Sabin Beast.
- [Fuel regulation readiness] Flex-fuel Splendor+ and HF Deluxe positioned as "future readiness", compatible with ethanol blends from E20 to E85.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 commodity cost pressure: ~₹2,000/unit increase; Price hike taken: ~2% (₹700-₹3,500/model) in April; Gap: High single-digit BOM cost increase vs 2% price hike creates short-term margin headwind; Mitigation: LEAP savings, volume leverage, discretionary spend cuts.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: High single-digit industry growth expected in FY27; Hero to outgrow industry; Margins: Medium-term guidance 14-16% maintained despite short-term transitory pressure from commodities; Order Inflow: Strong momentum continuing into FY27; Capex: ₹1,500 cr committed for FY27 (Scooter/EV capacity, Parts center).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Channel inventory healthy at ~5 weeks (down YoY); EV inventory specifically in single-digit days; Retail performance outpaced wholesale indicating demand pull-through.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scooterization trend (gaining share in 100-125cc); EV penetration (currently ~7% of industry, targeting 90% PLI coverage); Export expansion (Latin America, Africa, Bangladesh/Sri Lanka penetration); Aftermarket parts (targeting unaddressed 50% gray market).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Hero MotoCorp delivered record FY26 revenue and PAT driven by a structural shift to scooters and exports, but faces immediate FY27 margin compression from West Asia-induced commodity spikes (aluminum/fuel) that outpace current 2% price hikes. The strategic pivot involves aggressive capacity doubling in scooters/EV and a ₹1,500 crore capex plan to capture high-growth segments while navigating a transitory profitability dip.

drhp.business: Hero MotoCorp manufactures two-wheelers - motorcycles and scooters - accounting for 100% of turnover per its BRSR business-activity disclosure. Its portfolio spans mass-market commuter and premium motorcycles, scooters, the VIDA electric-vehicle brand and charging ecosystem, a premium motorcycle line developed with Harley-Davidson, and a Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business, serving customers across India and 52 other countries.
drhp.expansion: The Company is transitioning its legacy manufacturing footprint to be more agile, redesigning capacity to favour a high-yield mix of Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles while continuing to grow commuter-motorcycle share. Its manufacturing base comprises six facilities in India (Gurugram, Dharuhera, Halol, Neemrana, Haridwar and Tirupati) plus dedicated overseas plants in Villa Rica, Colombia (its first overseas manufacturing facility) and Jessore, Bangladesh (a joint venture with the Niloy Group), together supporting an approximate annual production capacity of 8.63 million …

litigation.note: Board's Report 'Update on Significant Matters': Income Tax Authorities disallowed certain prior-period expenses and raised a demand; the Company is appealing to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) and, based on external legal advice, believes no provision is required. Separately, past government-agency investigations were concluded favourably, with no material adjustments or disclosures identified as of the date of approval of the financial statements. The Statutory Auditor's Report (standalone and consolidated) remains unmodified.
